voiceover: Before a website sends you a single pixel, your computer and the server do a handshake. That's literally what it's called. Step one, TCP: your computer says SYN, the server says SYN-ACK, you say ACK. Now you're connected. Step two, TLS, the S in HTTPS. The server shows a certificate proving it really is that domain, and both sides agree on encryption keys so nobody in between can read your traffic. That's what the lock icon means: private connection, right domain. It doesn't mean the site is honest. People misread it so much that one major browser replaced it. Part three: finally, the actual page.
